faq.title: Everything you need to know about customs clearance via Iran
faq.sub: Straight answers to the questions importers and exporters ask us most.

home.faq.q: Do you clear goods coming from Iran into Iraq?
home.faq.a: Yes. Al-Bait Al-Iraqi for Customs Clearance is based at the Zurbatiyah border crossing in Wasit, Iraq, directly opposite Iran's Mehran crossing. We clear goods imported from Iran and transit cargo moving through Iran via every land crossing between Iraq and Iran, and we also handle exports from Iraq to Iran.

home.faq.q: Which Iraq–Iran border crossings do you work at?
home.faq.a: All official land crossings: Zurbatiyah–Mehran, Al-Sheeb–Chazabeh, Shalamcheh, Al-Mundhiriya–Khosravi, Haj Omran–Tamarchin, Bashmakh–Bashmaq and Parwezkhan–Parviz Khan. We also follow shipments arriving from Iranian ports such as Bandar Abbas and Bandar Imam Khomeini.

home.faq.q: How long does customs clearance take at Zurbatiyah?
home.faq.a: Our average is about 3 working days after the truck arrives and the documents are complete. It varies with the type of goods, inspections and permits. We review your documents before shipping to avoid delays.

home.faq.q: What documents do I need to import goods from Iran into Iraq?
home.faq.a: Usually: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, transport document (CMR for road or bill of lading for sea), an Iraqi import licence where required, a certificate of conformity (COC) for regulated goods, and a health or phytosanitary certificate for food. We review the documents before shipping to avoid fines and delays.

home.faq.q: Can I ship goods from China to Iraq via Iran?
home.faq.a: Yes — it is a common route. Containers are discharged at Shahid Rajaee Port in Bandar Abbas, travel overland through Iran under transit to Mehran–Zurbatiyah, Shalamcheh or another crossing, and we clear them through customs on entry into Iraq.

home.faq.q: Do you also clear exports from Iraq to Iran?
home.faq.a: Yes. We handle export formalities — export declarations, certificates of origin and coordination with the relevant authorities — for products such as Iraqi dates.

home.faq.q: What kinds of goods do you clear?
home.faq.a: All commercial goods: foodstuffs, steel and building materials, marble, heavy machinery, and specialised cargo such as medical and chemical materials, including the permits they require.

home.faq.q: How do I get a customs clearance quote?
home.faq.a: Send your shipment details (goods, weight, border crossing) on WhatsApp to +964 775 168 7406 or through the form on this website, and we will send you a quote within 24 hours.

home.faq.q: Where is your office and what are your working hours?
home.faq.a: Our office is at the Zurbatiyah border crossing, Badra district, Wasit Governorate, Iraq. We work Sunday to Thursday, 8:00 to 17:00, and you can reach us on WhatsApp or at support@iqbait.com.
More than 11 years of experience since 2015, over 3,000 shipments cleared between Iraq and Iran, a permanent presence at the Zurbatiyah crossing, and follow-up at every step from request to release.

guide.h1: Iran–Iraq customs clearance guide: border crossings, ports, documents and steps

We clear goods between Iran and Iraq through all seven land border crossings and via Iranian seaports — imports, exports and transit — with an average clearance time of 3 working days. guide.howTitle: How does customs clearance between Iran and Iraq work?
guide.howText: Every shipment goes through two stages: exit or transit formalities on the Iranian side, then customs clearance on entry into Iraq. On the Iraqi side, the customs broker files the declaration on the importer's behalf; the goods are then inspected and valued, and duties are paid before release. Choosing the right crossing and preparing the documents before loading save the most time and money.
guide.crossTitle: The seven land border crossings between Iraq and Iran
guide.routes: Baghdad and central Iraq: Zurbatiyah–Mehran or Al-Mundhiriya–Khosravi.
Maysan and the southern provinces: Al-Sheeb–Chazabeh.
Kurdistan Region: Haj Omran–Tamarchin (Erbil), Bashmakh–Bashmaq (Sulaymaniyah) and Parwezkhan.
Containers from China and Asia: Shahid Rajaee Port (Bandar Abbas), then overland transit to the crossing nearest your destination.

guide.steps.name: Send the documents for review
guide.steps.text: Send the invoice, packing list and certificate of origin before loading so we can check the goods description, tariff lines and required approvals.

guide.steps.name: Obtain the approvals
guide.steps.text: We identify whether your shipment needs an import licence, a certificate of conformity (COC) or health and agricultural certificates, and follow them up.

guide.steps.name: Truck arrival and declaration
guide.steps.text: When the goods reach the crossing, we file the customs declaration in your name and register the shipment.

guide.steps.name: Inspection and valuation
guide.steps.text: The goods are inspected and matched against the documents, and their customs value is set.

guide.steps.name: Paying duties
guide.steps.text: Customs duties and taxes are paid according to the tariff in force, and we send you the details.

guide.steps.name: Release
guide.steps.text: The goods are released to continue to their destination in Iraq, and we notify you as soon as clearance is complete.

guide.docs.name: Commercial invoice
guide.docs.text: An accurate description, quantity and value of the goods.

guide.docs.name: Packing list
guide.docs.text: Weights and package counts that match the invoice.

guide.docs.name: Certificate of origin
guide.docs.text: Proof of the goods' country of origin.

guide.docs.name: Transport document
guide.docs.text: CMR for road transport or a bill of lading for sea freight.

guide.docs.name: Import licence
guide.docs.text: For goods that require one under Iraqi regulations.

guide.docs.name: Certificate of conformity (COC)
guide.docs.text: For goods covered by the pre-shipment quality inspection programme.

guide.docs.name: Health and agricultural certificates
guide.docs.text: For foodstuffs and agricultural or animal products.

guide.docsNote: Requirements depend on the goods. Send us your document list and we will tell you what is missing before you ship.
guide.timeTitle: How long does it take and what does it cost?
guide.timeText: Our average clearance time is 3 working days after the goods arrive and the documents are complete; goods that need inspections or special approvals can take longer. Duties are calculated from the Iraqi customs tariff and the type and value of the goods, so we send you a detailed quote within 24 hours of receiving your shipment details.
guide.tipsTitle: Tips to avoid delays and fines
guide.tips: Match weights and quantities across the invoice, packing list and transport document.
Describe the goods precisely rather than using general terms.
Get the certificate of conformity and approvals before loading, not after arrival.
Make sure the certificate of origin matches the invoice.
Choose the crossing closest to the goods' destination in Iraq.
Send us copies of the documents for review before the truck leaves.

guide.faq.q: What is the difference between importing from Iran and transit through Iran?
guide.faq.a: With an import, the goods are of Iranian origin and are exported directly from Iran. With transit, the goods come from a third country such as China or Turkey and cross Iranian territory without entering the Iranian market. In both cases, Iraqi customs clearance takes place at the crossing where the goods enter Iraq.

guide.faq.q: Does my shipment need follow-up on the Iranian side?
guide.faq.a: Yes. The shipment must complete exit or transit formalities on the Iranian side. We follow up and coordinate this until the goods reach the Iraqi crossing, then clear them — so you deal with a single contact.

guide.faq.q: Which crossing is best for my shipment?
guide.faq.a: It depends on the destination in Iraq: Zurbatiyah–Mehran or Al-Mundhiriya–Khosravi for Baghdad and central Iraq, Shalamcheh for Basra, Al-Sheeb–Chazabeh for Maysan and the south, and Haj Omran, Bashmakh or Parwezkhan for the Kurdistan Region. We help you pick the shortest route and the quickest clearance.

guide.faq.q: Can my goods be cleared without me being at the crossing?
guide.faq.a: Yes. Once we receive the documents and the required authorisation, we complete the formalities on your behalf and update you on WhatsApp at every stage until release.
